walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordination & Response — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordination & Response brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordination & Response.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a prokaryote?
options: Human skin cell
Yeast
Bacterium
Onion cell
protein synthesis
photosynthesis
aerobic respiration
cell division

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a silent and a missense mutation?
options: A silent mutation has no effect because no base actually changes.
Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
A silent mutation changes a base but the codon still codes for the same amino acid; a missense mutation changes the amino acid encoded.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.

mcqs.q: After pre-mRNA splicing in eukaryotes, which sequences remain in the mature mRNA?
options: Introns remain because they encode the protein; exons are removed as junk.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Exons remain; introns are removed.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
